routes.name: Tourist entry permit
routes.summary: Many nationalities enter Peru without a visa and get a tourist stay set by the border officer, up to 183 days. It can't be extended. Overstaying costs US$1 per extra day, paid when you leave.

other: Visa-free list depends on nationality. Check the official Peruvian foreign ministry list before you travel.
Exact visa-free country list not confirmed from an official page.

stay.note: Days are set by the migration officer at entry.

routes.name: Temporary visa (Visa Temporal)
routes.summary: Applied for from inside Peru through a local representative. Authorizes up to 90 days, extendable to one year. The visa is then placed in your passport at a Peruvian consulate abroad and residence is formalized.

other: Requirements depend on the activity (work, family, study, investment). Exact lists not confirmed from an official page.

stay.note: Up to 90 days, extendable to one year per Migraciones guidance.

routes.name: Permanent visa (Visa Permanente)
routes.summary: Same process as the temporary visa. Migraciones describes it as an authorization of up to one year, renewable. The official text doesn't explain how it differs in practice, so check with Migraciones.

other: Requirements not confirmed from an official page.

routes.name: Change of migratory status (Cambio de Calidad Migratoria)
routes.summary: If you're already in Peru legally, for example as a tourist, you can ask to change to a status that lets you work, invest or live there. Approval goes on your Carne de Extranjeria. Family already in Peru can be included. You can leave for up to 30 days while it's pending, but only with a special travel permit.

other: Must be in Peru in a regular status.
Requirements depend on the category. Fees and exact documents not confirmed from an official page.

steps: File the change of status request with Migraciones.
Get a Permiso Especial para Viajar before leaving the country while it's pending.
Once approved, get your Carne de Extranjeria.

routes.name: Worker (Trabajador) and designated worker (Trabajador designado)
routes.summary: Trabajador is for people entering to work under a contract approved by the Ministry of Labor. Trabajador designado is for people sent by a foreign employer for a fixed period without intent to reside. Tourists can also request a change of status to work.

other: Contract must be approved by the Ministry of Labor and Employment Promotion.
Durations, fees and full requirements not confirmed from an official page.

routes.name: Annual residence renewal (Prorroga de Residencia)
routes.summary: Residence from a visa or status change is renewed every year, with the annual foreigner fee. Residence is cancelled if you're out of Peru more than 183 days in any 12 months, unless you get an absence authorization for force majeure.

other: Fee amounts not confirmed from an official page.

stay.note: Absence over 183 days in a 12-month period cancels residence.

routes.name: Mercosur residence agreement
routes.summary: Mercosur nationals can get legal residence by proving their country of birth and meeting the agreement's requirements. Temporary residence runs up to two years. You can convert it to permanent residence if you apply within 90 days before it expires.

other: Exact member list and documents not confirmed from the cited page.

routes.name: Andean Community worker rights (Decision 545)
routes.summary: Andean migrant workers get equal treatment and job opportunities. Before signing a contract, they need a permit from Migraciones. They can ID with a passport or their national ID card. The employer registers the contract online in SIVITMA and handles the status change.

other: Applies to Andean Community nationals under Decision 545.
